intro.title: Before goals, tell the story of {lastYear}
intro.body: Mudmai runs on a calendar year, January–December. We’ll keep your story, joy, learnings, and what healed you — so the AI companion can recall them when this year gets heavy.
intro.aiBadge: The AI companion remembers what healed you
intro.pillarsHint: These six colors are the life pillars — you’ll see them across the app.

lastYearStory.title: Tell me about your last year
lastYearStory.hint: It doesn’t need to be polished. It needs to be yours — two or three moments are enough.
lastYearStory.placeholder: e.g. {lastYear} started heavy at work… mid-year I finally rested… by the end I felt…
lastYearStory.guideIntro: Tell a short story. You don’t have to cover the whole year — keep what still sits with you.
prompts: Overall, did last year rise, dip, or stay flat?
What stood out in work, money, people, or health?
Was there a stretch that felt especially hard — or proud?
Looking back now, what do you want to remember?
lastYearStory.examplesHint: Not the “right” answer — just tones you can steal. Write yours.

examples.label: Short and direct
examples.body: Work ate most of the year. I switched teams mid-year and could breathe again. Family felt closer because I went home more. Health slipped a little, but I feel sturdier than I did in January.

examples.label: As a story
examples.body: I meant to run and save. Q1 buried both. A three-day trip with friends in the middle of the year showed me I wasn’t resting at all. I started sleeping earlier near the end. Not perfect — but I had a place to stand again.

examples.label: As bullets
examples.body: Work: a big project, then burnout. Money: survived, didn’t save. People: drifted from old friends, closer to family. Heart: chronic stress, lighter in the last stretch.

happiestMoment.title: Happiest stretch or moment last year
happiestMoment.hint: People, work, travel, or a quiet patch of peace.
happiestMoment.placeholder: e.g. The happiest stretch was… because of a person / place / feeling…
happiestMoment.guideIntro: It doesn’t have to be a big trip. A light day counts.
prompts: Who were you with — or were you alone?
What did it feel like in your body — ease, warmth, pride?
Why does that moment still sit in your head?
happiestMoment.examplesHint: Short or long is fine. Keep the picture you actually remember.

examples.label: A quiet one
examples.body: A Saturday morning making coffee slowly, no notifications. Life didn’t have to rush.

examples.label: People
examples.body: Dinner with family after a long gap. We retold the same old stories and I knew that’s what I’d been missing.

keyLearnings.title: What did you learn about yourself?
keyLearnings.hint: The insight you want to carry into this year.
keyLearnings.placeholder: e.g. I learned that I… and this year I don’t want to repeat…
keyLearnings.guideIntro: No fortune-cookie wisdom needed — just what last year made clearer about you.
prompts: What did you think you could handle — and couldn’t?
What scared you, that you did anyway?
Which sentence do you want to carry this year?
keyLearnings.examplesHint: One true sentence beats ten pretty ones.

examples.label: Boundaries
examples.body: I’m good when I have edges. If I say yes to everything, the work and my heart break together.

examples.label: Rest
examples.body: Rest isn’t a prize after the work is done — without it, the work never finishes anyway.

healingThings.title: What healed you?
healingThings.hint: Activities, people, or coping that restored you — the companion will recall this if mental or career scores drop.
healingThings.placeholder: e.g. When my heart is heavy I… (walk, call a friend, cook, put the phone away…)
healingThings.guideIntro: Whatever actually brings you back. The companion will recall this when the year gets heavy.
prompts: When you’re stressed, what actually helps?
Who or which place holds you up?
Is there a tiny daily ritual that works?
healingThings.examplesHint: The more specific, the better the later nudge.

examples.label: Activities
examples.body: A twenty-minute walk without headphones, a slow shower, three lines in a notebook before bed.

examples.label: People and ritual
examples.body: Calling my sister with no need for answers — just telling the day — and cooking even a simple dinner.

ratings.title: How did each pillar feel in {lastYear}?
ratings.hint: Slide with how it felt. Color and shape follow you — you don’t have to think in numbers first.

expectationsNextYear.title: What do you expect this year?
expectationsNextYear.hint: A feeling, a direction, or the picture you want at year-end.
expectationsNextYear.placeholder: e.g. In {activeYear} I want to feel… and by December I want to see myself…
expectationsNextYear.guideIntro: This isn’t a SMART list yet — a feeling or a picture is enough.
prompts: How do you want to feel at year-end?

Is there one picture you want to come true?
expectationsNextYear.examplesHint: Direction is enough. Details can wait for SMART goals.

examples.label: A feeling
examples.body: I want to finish the year not emptied out, close to people I love, proud that small things happened steadily.

examples.label: A year-end picture
examples.body: An emergency fund, weekly walks back in my body, and work that doesn’t swallow the whole of life.

pdpa.title: Privacy notice
pdpa.intro: Mudmai stores what you enter so you can plan a calendar year, reflect, track goals, and receive gentle reminders. We do not sell your data. LINE news and promotions are sent only if you turn that switch on.
pdpa.collectBody: Account: email or LINE login identifier, display name, language, timezone, PDPA consent · LINE userId when you sign in or connect the OA · Last-year reflection: story, happiest moment, learnings, what healed you, next-year hopes, and 1–5 ratings across six pillars (including mental and physical health) · Vision board: text, uploaded images, drawings · SMART goals, milestones, daily todos, monthly/quarterly reviews, reminder preferences, and AI nudge messages.
pdpa.purposeBody: To create your account, sync to the cloud, render your dashboard, send in-app/browser reminders, send private cadence reminders through the LINE Official Account when you connect and opt in, and write companion nudges that recall what you said healed you — we do not use LINE Notify.
pdpa.lineBody: We store your LINE userId to sign you in and to send private cadence messages. News, promotions, and referral campaigns are a separate opt-in (off by default). You can block the OA or withdraw consent any time. Health scores and healing text are never placed in LINE messages.
pdpa.sensitiveBody: Mental/physical health ratings and healing text can be sensitive under PDPA. We store them because they power reflection and nudges, and only after you consent.
pdpa.retentionBody: We keep data while your account exists, or until you delete it. In demo mode, data stays in this browser (localStorage) and is not uploaded.
pdpa.rightsBody: You can access and export JSON from Settings, and delete in-app data with Delete account. If a service-role key is configured, the auth user is removed too; otherwise app rows are deleted and you are signed out.
pdpa.aiBody: If OPENAI_API_KEY is set, short nudge copy may be generated on the server from text you wrote (for example what healed you). We do not use it to train our own models. Without a key, the app uses local templates.
pdpa.disclaimer: This is an in-app notice, not legal advice. For data questions, contact whoever operates this deployment.
pdpa.consentSubtitle: Please read the notice, then agree so we can store and use your data as described.
